claim: An apply whose every edit names a path git ignores makes no commit and takes the file off the disk all the same. The answer says nothing was committed, which reads as nothing having happened, and the repository's history records the write nowhere. An agent reading that answer, or anyone reading the log after, has no way to learn from either that a file went.

evidence:
I ran `akasha change draft remove-file` with `at: change/mechanical/file-content/remove/remove-page-property/remove-page-property.change-mechanical-file-content.entries.uncommitted.jsonl`, a 73409-byte file git does not track, and then `akasha change apply`. The whole answer was two lines:

`folded change/mechanical/file-content/remove/remove-page-property/remove-page-property.change-mechanical-file-content.entries.uncommitted.jsonl in`
`nothing was committed, because git ignores the path(s) this apply took away: change/mechanical/file-content/remove/remove-page-property/remove-page-property.change-mechanical-file-content.entries.uncommitted.jsonl`

Listing the folder after that apply showed three files where there had been four. The file was gone. `git log` names no commit for it, because there is none, and the kept edits were cleared, so nothing beside the agent's page records it either.

The two readings this sits between: an apply that writes the disk and commits, which the log records; and an apply that is refused, which writes nothing. This is a third, and its answer's first word is the word a landing uses — `folded … in` — while its second sentence says nothing was committed. Reading the second sentence as "nothing happened" is the mistake available here, and I made it far enough to have to go and look at the folder to find out.

What it is worth is for whoever picks it up. The write may be right and only the saying wrong, in which case the answer could name what went off the disk rather than only why no commit was made. Or an apply over only ignored paths could be refused, on the ground that a change the repository cannot record is not a change this system should make. I did not mend it.
